target.title: docs(slack): clarify group DM bot membership
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a docs gap where Slack users can read the `dm.groupEnabled` and
`dm.groupChannels` settings and reasonably assume those settings can make
OpenClaw see an existing group DM after someone mentions the bot.

Slack group DMs (MPDMs) do not work that way: if the app is not already a
member of the MPDM, Slack does not deliver the conversation to the app.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a Slack docs subsection explaining that `@YourBot` in an existing
group DM does not add the app or make the MPDM visible to it. It also clarifies
that `dm.groupEnabled` and `dm.groupChannels` only filter MPDMs Slack already
delivers, and it links that explanation from the channel config reference.

The documented workarounds are the Slack-supported paths: convert the group DM
to a private channel and invite the app, or have the app open a new MPDM with
`conversations.open`.

## User Impact

Operators get a clearer answer when Slack group-DM routing appears broken: no
OpenClaw config can grant visibility into an MPDM the app never joined. The docs
now point users to the two working setup paths instead of leaving them to chase
`dm.groupEnabled` / `dm.groupChannels` as a fix.

## Evidence

- AI-assisted docs PR prepared by Codex, with a Claude Foreman Opus review pass
  before push.
- Docs-only change.
- Ran `pnpm docs:list` before editing docs.
- Ran `pnpm check:docs`:
  - `format:docs:check`
  - `lint:docs`
  - `docs:check-mdx`
  - `docs:check-i18n-glossary`
  - `docs:check-links`
  - `docs:map:check`
- Regenerated `docs/docs_map.md` with `pnpm docs:map:gen`.
- Ran `git diff --check`.
- Verified the public diff contains no private Slack channel IDs, local project
  paths, or security-advisory details.
- Reviewed by Claude Foreman on Opus before push. Foreman flagged the original
  workaround wording as too broad, so the final text now uses the narrower
  documented bot-token `conversations.open` path.
